name: Memory
description: Persistent cross-session memory plus per-session short-term scratchpad. Saves via the inline <ma::emit::memory> tag (zero-friction, mid-response); reads/edits/removes via the MemoryTool (structured CRUD by id). Three scopes: global (~/.minimal-agent/memory.md), project (~/.minimal-agent/projects/<cwd>/memory.md), short-term (~/.minimal-agent/sessions/<sid>.scratch.md). Persistent scopes are not injected into the system prompt by default (use `MemoryTool({action: "list"})` to query); short-term rides as a per-turn user-message attachment.

tool.name: MemoryTool
tool.description: List, read, add, edit, or remove saved memories. Memories are not shown in your system prompt by default; use this tool to query them whenever a saved lesson might apply (debugging a familiar symptom, recalling a user's preferences, looking up prior solutions on this codebase). Three scopes: `global` (cross-project, about working with this user), `project` (about this codebase), `short-term` (this session only). For in-flight saves mid-response, prefer the inline <ma::emit::memory> tag (lower friction, save-echo returns the id next turn). `list` is paginated: default returns the most recent 20 entries with body previews clipped to ~160 chars; the header includes a paste-ready `next: MemoryTool({...})` hint for the next page. Use `read` to fetch the full body of a specific bullet by id. `id` is required for read/edit/remove; `body` for add/edit; `query`/`limit`/`offset` are list-only. `clear` is only allowed for scope=short-term.

scope.description: Which memory file to act on.

id.description: Bullet id from a prior <memory-saved> echo, list result, or save-echo. Required for read/edit/remove. Persistent ids look like `lwq8tg-a8f3`; short-term ids are integers like `3`.

body.description: New body for add or edit. Single-line preferred; multi-line is collapsed to one line.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter for action=list. Pairs with limit/offset for filtered pagination.

limit.description: For action=list, page size. Default 20, max 100 (over-large values are clamped). Pair with `offset` to page through the full set.

offset.description: For action=list, number of entries to skip counted FROM THE NEWEST END. offset=0 (default) returns the most recent page; offset=20 returns the page before that, and so on. The response header's `next:` hint shows the exact value for the next page.

format.description: Result format. `text` (default) returns a compact human-readable list. `json` returns a structured shape suitable when you need to extract specific values.

tool.reason: tool name already includes plugin identity (Memory)
